Here’s a complete outline you can keep in front of you during the call.

--------------------------------
1. Verification & Reason for Call
--------------------------------
When they ask how they can help:

“Hi, I need to dispute a duplicate charge on my credit card.

The card is my main credit card ending in 4421. On November 2, 2025, there are two charges from Best Buy for $249.99. I only made one purchase that day.

Please open a dispute for the extra charge:
- Transaction ID: TXN-004  
- Merchant: Best Buy  
- Amount: $249.99  
- Date: November 2, 2025  

Please leave the other transaction, TXN-001, as the valid charge and treat TXN-004 as the duplicate.”

--------------------------------
2. Short Summary Paragraph
--------------------------------
After that, you can add:

“Just to summarize: this was a single in‑store purchase at Best Buy for $249.99. I only checked out once, and my receipt shows only one transaction. However, my statement shows two identical charges on November 2, 2025. I’d like you to treat TXN‑001 as the correct charge and open a dispute on TXN‑004 as a duplicate. I still have the in‑store receipt and can provide a copy if you need it. I don’t believe I need a new card, just the duplicate charge reversed.”

--------------------------------
3. Common Questions & Quick Answers
--------------------------------
If they ask common questions, you can answer:

• Did you make this purchase, and how many times?  
“Yes, I made one in‑store purchase at Best Buy for $249.99 on that date. There are two identical charges, but I only made one purchase.”

• Which transaction is correct and which is the duplicate?  
“Please treat TXN-001 as the correct charge and TXN-004 as the duplicate that I’m disputing.”

• Do you see both charges on your receipt?  
“No. My in‑store receipt shows only one purchase for $249.99, not two.”

• Did the merchant run the card more than once?  
“Not that I’m aware of. At the store, I checked out once and the payment went through normally.”

• Have you contacted Best Buy?  
Use whichever applies:  
“Not yet. I saw there are two identical charges and wanted to report it to you right away.”  
—or—  
“Yes, I contacted Best Buy and they said I should dispute the duplicate with my bank.”

• Do you have supporting documents?  
“Yes, I still have the in‑store receipt showing only one transaction for $249.99. I can provide a copy if needed.”

• Was this in‑store or online?  
“It was an in‑store purchase at Best Buy.”

• Do you want a new card issued?  
“No, I recognize the merchant and this looks like a duplicate processing issue. I don’t think I need a new card, just the duplicate charge reversed.”

--------------------------------
4. If They Tell You to Contact Best Buy First
--------------------------------
If they say “You should contact Best Buy first”:

“I understand. Since this is a duplicate charge on my credit card, I’d still like to open a formal dispute on your side so the investigation is documented. I do have my in‑store receipt showing only one purchase for $249.99. Could you please open the dispute while I also follow up with Best Buy if needed?”

If they push back:

“I’m happy to reach out to Best Buy, but I’d like this documented as a dispute now so the timelines and protections on my credit card are in place.”

--------------------------------
5. If They Don’t See the Second Charge Yet
--------------------------------
If they say “I only see one charge”:

“On my side I’m seeing two Best Buy charges for $249.99 dated November 2, 2025, with transaction IDs TXN‑001 and TXN‑004. Could you please double‑check recent and pending activity for my card ending in 4421?”

If they still don’t see it:

“In that case, I’ll take screenshots and check again later today. If both charges are still showing on my account and on your end, I’ll call back to open the dispute for TXN‑004 as the duplicate. In the meantime, I’d like it noted on my account that I reported a potential duplicate charge today.”

--------------------------------
6. Before You Hang Up
--------------------------------
Before ending the call, ask:

“Can you please give me the dispute case number and a brief summary of what will happen next and when I should expect an update?”
